Case Study: Streaming Watch Habits

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A video-streaming service surveyed 200 of its subscribers to understand viewing habits. Each subscriber was asked two things: whether they had watched the platform's award-winning documentary, and whether they held a Premium subscription rather than the free ad-supported plan. The results were entered into a two-way table. Of the 100 Premium subscribers, 60 had watched the documentary and 40 had not. Among the 100 free-plan subscribers, only 30 had watched it while 70 had not. The marketing team wants to use these figures to test claims such as “Premium members are more likely to watch our original films” and to decide whether watching the documentary and holding a Premium plan are statistically independent. They compute several conditional probabilities directly from the counts in the table.

questions.q: Are “holds Premium” and “watched the documentary” independent?
options: It cannot be decided from a table
Not independent, since P(P∩ W)≠ P(P) P(W)
questions.explanation: P(Prem) P(Doc)=100/200·90/200=0.225, but P(Prem∩ Doc)=60/200=0.3≠0.225, so they are not independent. (d).
